title: ACME Fintech audit runbook and sample evidence
summary: Working runbook and evidence index created during the ACME Fintech POC security kickoff and workshop. Purpose: provide an ordered checklist for responding to ACME's infosec questionnaire, map requested controls to available artifacts, and surface any outstanding gaps for engineering and product teams to remediate prior to customer audit. This is a living document; use the linked S3 folder as the canonical artifact store and update statuses below.
evidence_index: Overview: below is a compact index of artifacts we've collected or will produce for ACME. Each line: artifact filename (where stored) — short description — owner — status. 1) redwood-architecture-acme-v1.pdf (s3://.../network-diagram-v1.pdf) — Logical architecture for ACME dedicated VPC deployment, includes transit gateways, private control plane notes — Owner: Ravi Patel — Status: final. 2) acme-net-acls-and-subnets.csv (s3://.../configs/) — Export of VPC subnet, ACLs, security groups used in the PoC infra — Owner: Jordan Reyes — Status: in_review. 3) key-management-diagram.png (s3://.../kms/) — Diagram showing KMS integration options (customer-managed CMK in AWS) and Redwood KMS usage — Owner: Elena Sokolov — Status: draft. 4) poc-pen-test-summary-2024.pdf (s3://.../thirdparty-reports/) — Third-party pentest high-level findings for our standard hosting config (redacted for customer) — Owner: Security Ops — Status: final. 5) data-flow-user-data-redaction.md (s3://.../docs/) — Notes on how PHI/PII is redacted or excluded from telemetry and telemetry retention — Owner: Maya Chen — Status: final. 6) sse-and-transport-evidence.txt — TLS configuration, cipher lists and cert rotation cadence exported from servers — Owner: Infra — Status: pending export. 7) runbook-acme-incident-response.md — PoC-tailored incident response steps and on-call contacts — Owner: SRE — Status: draft. 8) qos-and-slo-report.csv — token-level latency/cost SLO run from PoC load test — Owner: Product Observability — Status: final.
control_mapping: High-level mapping to common controls requested by ACME: - SOC2 CC6.1 (Encryption in transit) -> artifact: sse-and-transport-evidence.txt, key-management-diagram.png; test: cert rotation log export. - SOC2 CC8.2 (Access provisioning) -> artifact: access-roles-acme-poc.csv (IAM roles & policies snapshot), linked in S3; owner: Infra. - SOC2 CC5.1 (Logging & monitoring) -> artifact: observability-config-export.json, alerting-runbook link; owner: Product Observability. - GDPR data processing (lawful basis & DPIA) -> artifact: dpa-dpia-acme.docx; owner: Legal. - PenTest evidence -> poc-pen-test-summary-2024.pdf + vuln-triage-jira IDs under SEC-8721. Notes: some artifacts are redacted versions; we will provide full copies under NDA/secure transfer. For each control mapped, next to it we maintain a one-line statement of sufficiency (Sufficient / Partial / Gap) in the shared S3 index file. Current quick status: Encryption in transit: Sufficient. Access provisioning: Partial (missing role attestation evidence). Logging & monitoring: Partial (need retention screenshots). GDPR DPIA: Sufficient (DPAs drafted, awaiting signature).
workshop_notes: Kickoff (2025-02-10) attendee notes and top-line takeaways: - ACME security lead (Nadine) emphasized requirement for customer-managed KMS for dedicated instances; asked for step-by-step setup doc. Action: produce KMS onboarding checklist and terraform snippet (Owner: Elena) - They want a short 1-page runbook that legal can ingest — not >2 pages. Action: generate 'ACME summary for legal' (Owner: Maya) - Data residency question: ACME insists PoC run in us-east-2 only. Infra will pin nodes and provide placement proof (Owner: Jordan). - Asked about SOC2 attestation timeline: they need our latest SOC2 Type II report; Security Ops to provide redacted copy and scope statement. - Workshop exercise: walked through a simulated model call with PII obfuscated. We iterated the prefix-trimming approach and documented the telemetry filters. Notes to devs: avoid logging raw prompt text to stdout in PoC build. - Unresolved: ACME asked for explicit SLA for 99.9% availability on dedicated pool for PoC; product needs to confirm whether we can commit for PoC or we provide documented reliability profile and fallback plan.
next_steps: Immediate (owners): 1) Elena: finalize KMS onboarding doc + terraform example (due 2025-02-17). 2) Jordan: export VPC & ACL CSV + placement proof screenshot (due 2025-02-14). 3) Security Ops: upload redacted SOC2 artefact to s3 path and confirm scope (due 2025-02-18). 4) Legal: prepare 1-page contract summary and DPA extract for ACME (due 2025-02-20). 5) SRE/Infra: produce cert-rotation logs and TLS config export (due 2025-02-21). Longer: schedule a follow-up workshop (30–60 minutes) to review the submitted artifacts with ACME security team; propose the week of 2025-02-24. Risks and blockers: SOC2 redaction timeline (may delay full evidence handoff), customer-managed KMS onboarding complexity (requires cross-team coordination), SLA ask (product decision). If any deliverable misses its date, flag in Jira SEC-8721 and escalate in weekly security sync.
